title_ar: شرح نخبة الفكر في مصطلح أهل الأثر الشريط السابع
title_en: Commentary on Nukhbat al-Fikr on the terminology of the people of hadith — tape seven
body_ar:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين اللهم افتح لنا بحكمتك وانشر علينا من رحمتك وأنزل علينا من بركاتك.

أما بعد فيقول الحافظ رحمه الله: " فإن قل عدده فإما أن ينتهي إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أو إلى إمام ذي صفة علية كشعبة فالأول العلو المطلق والثاني النسبي" هذا التقسيم الذي بدأه الحافظ هنا يسمى تقسيم الحديث باعتبار عدد الناقلين وباعتبار عدد الطبقات، وهو قسم من أقسام الحديث باعتبار عدد الناقلين، باعتبار عدد الناقلين أي عدد الطبقات، قال: فإن قل عدده أي إن قل عدد الإسناد وذلك مثل ثلاثيات البخاري التي يرويها البخاري عن المكي بن إبراهيم عن يزيد بن أبي عبيد عن سلمة بن الأكوع، وأولها في صحيح البخاري قول البخاري رحمه الله حدثنا المكي بن إبراهيم قال حدثنا يزيد بن أبي عبيد عن سلمة بن الأكوع قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: من يقل علي ما لم أقل فليتبوأ مقعده من النار..
body_en:
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. O God, open for us by Your wisdom, and spread over us of Your mercy, and send down upon us of Your blessings.

To proceed: al-Hafiz, may God have mercy on him, says: "And if its number is few, then it either ends at the Prophet, upon whom be God's blessing and peace, or at an imam possessed of an exalted quality, such as Shuʿbah; the first is absolute elevation and the second relative." This division, which al-Hafiz begins here, is called the division of the hadith by the number of transmitters and by the number of layers; it is one of the divisions of the hadith by the number of transmitters — by the number of transmitters, that is, the number of layers. He said: "and if its number is few", that is, if the number of the chain is few. That is like the three-link chains of al-Bukhari, which al-Bukhari narrates from al-Makki ibn Ibrahim, from Yazid ibn Abi ʿUbayd, from Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ. The first of them in the Ṣaḥīḥ of al-Bukhari is al-Bukhari's words, may God have mercy on him: "al-Makki ibn Ibrahim narrated to us; he said, Yazid ibn Abi ʿUbayd narrated to us, from Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, upon whom be God's blessing and peace, say: Whoever says of me what I did not say, let him take his seat in the Fire."..

flags.context: the two kinds of elevation of a chain of transmission
options: absolute and relative shortness of the chain
flags.note: ʿUluww is the technical quality of a chain that reaches its end-point through fewer intermediaries than usual, and is prized for that reason. 'Elevation' is the conventional English rendering and has been used. Note that muṭlaq here means 'absolute' as against 'relative', and is not the glossary's uṣūl sense of muṭlaq, 'unqualified' as against muqayyad. That homonym recurs in this corpus and should be added to the glossary's note on muṭlaq.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

This record belongs to the Sheikh's commentary on Ibn Hajar al-ʿAsqalani's Nukhbat al-Fikr, a short manual of hadith terminology. The CMS holds the tapes out of order across ids 628–637 and the tape numbers in the titles do not run with the ids; the series should be ordered by the tape number in the title, not by id, and even then a gap remains (see the note on the download filenames).

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text is the opening of a lecture and breaks off; the full transcript is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.
'The three-link chains of al-Bukhari' renders thulāthiyyāt al-Bukhārī — the reports in his Ṣaḥīḥ that reach the Prophet through only three narrators, his shortest chains.

'An imam possessed of an exalted quality' renders imām dhī ṣifah ʿaliyyah: a figure of such standing that reaching him by a short chain is itself a distinction, which is what makes the elevation relative rather than absolute. Shuʿbah is Shuʿbah ibn al-Hajjaj.
The opening supplication is a recited text; the Arabic is the operative form and is kept alongside the English rendering of its meaning.

The repetition in 'by the number of transmitters — by the number of transmitters, that is, the number of layers' is in the source; it is the Sheikh correcting himself mid-sentence in a spoken lecture, and has been kept rather than tidied away.
